mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT raises weekday trip chains into central retail areas, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. If commuting mobility keeps improving while residential time stays elevated, retail visits should follow with a lag.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the prior four-week mean after a further 2+ point improvement in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT over the next month.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline while PARKS mobility drops from the prior week, households substitute away from local discretionary outings and into home-based activity, reducing RETAIL_REC within one to two weeks. The effect is strongest when both signals move in opposite directions.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below its prior-week value after RESIDENTIAL stays above 0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days despite RESIDENTIAL staying positive and PARKS declining from the previous week.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT continues to sit far below baseline, retail access remains constrained and RETAIL_REC stays depressed over the next four weeks. A persistent transit gap signals unresolved mobility restrictions or avoidance that directly suppresses shopping and dining trips.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -40 for two consecutive weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases above its last-four-week average while TRANSIT stays below -40 for two more weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS alongside milder grocery and pharmacy mobility indicates improved weather and outdoor circulation, which spills over into discretionary retail visits over the next one to two weeks. The signal should weaken if the park rebound is isolated and does not persist.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises at least 5 points above the prior week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days after a PARKS rebound of at least 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: A further narrowing of the gap between WORKPLACES and TRANSIT predicts higher RETAIL_REC because more commuting converts into incidental shopping and eating out. The mechanism acts over about four weeks, not immediately, as routine travel patterns normalize.
candidate_trigger: the WORKPLACES minus TRANSIT gap shrinks by at least 10 points from its current level
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below the previous four-week mean even after the WORKPLACES-TRANSIT gap narrows by 10 points.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM stays close to baseline while RETAIL_REC remains negative, consumers are concentrating spending on essentials and delaying discretionary trips. That pattern should keep retail-and-recreation mobility flat or lower over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 7 days while GROCERY_PHARM remains between -10 and 0.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES rebounds while RESIDENTIAL remains only mildly elevated, the city is likely easing movement limits enough to restore discretionary trips. Under that regime, retail mobility should improve within two weeks as daytime circulation resumes.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -15 while RESIDENTIAL stays between 0 and 8
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve within 14 days after WORKPLACES exceeds -15 and RESIDENTIAL stays in the 0 to 8 range.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained improvement in PARKS combined with a parallel rise in TRANSIT implies broader citywide movement confidence, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The effect fails if parks rise alone without any transit recovery.
candidate_trigger: PARKS and TRANSIT both rise for two consecutive weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-four-week average after two weeks of simultaneous gains in PARKS and TRANSIT.
